items.title: Adaptive next-action and mastery reliability
items.acceptance: A learner's own evidence changes what they are asked to do, in the direction the pedagogy claims; the mastery threshold that gates prerequisites and stages separates durable answers from fragile ones, and the measurement reports where it fails.
evidence: npm run reliability: held-out mastery Brier 0.276 vs the learner-own-rate baseline 0.311 (n=327); the 0.65 threshold separates 65.3% correct among established calls from 49.1% among not-yet calls
npm run benchmark: 43 learners; plan names a documented weak concept 76.7%, top action is one 25.6%, coverage 40.5%; 90-learner cohort, 0 invariant violations; 52 of 90 return to a weak concept
Benchmark reports 1 named adversarial capability gap and 4/8 Section G hint-reliance cells not held; hint reliance is invisible below the established bar
The conventional specification-order rule scores 0.0% on the weak-concept question by construction; that is a structural difference, not a learning gain
items.remainingWork: Both instruments use a seeded synthetic cohort. Neither measures whether following the recommendation improves learning; that needs real learners, a baseline and a delayed test. One adversarial expectation and four hint-reliance cells remain unresolved and must not be reported as full adaptive validity.
